mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trip chains stay weak and discretionary shopping demand falls further, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay below their last-4-week means and RESIDENTIAL stays above its last-4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility signals more out-of-home leisure activity and spillover stop-making, which lifts retail-and-recreation visits within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above its prior 4-week average after a decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after PARKS turns up from a lower 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall sharply in the same week, it indicates a renewed restriction or avoidance shock that suppresses shopping trips and reduces RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT or WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days after a week with simultaneous sharp drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent level reflects more errand-based trips and neighborhood circulation, which usually precedes higher retail-and-recreation mobility within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM is above its own 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while PARKS and TRANSIT remain weak, households are substituting toward at-home time and away from discretionary outings, so retail-and-recreation mobility continues to soften over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above baseline by more than 10 points for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +10 and both PARKS and TRANSIT staying below their recent averages.

mechanism_narrative: A short-term jump in PARKS after a weak month signals favorable weather or seasonal outdoor substitution, which diverts time from indoor shopping and lowers RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS jumps by at least 8 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days after a week-on-week PARKS jump of at least 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains deeply negative while GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES recover only modestly, mobility is fragmenting rather than normalizing, and retail recovery stalls or reverses over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -45 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -45 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: During reopening, a concurrent improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT raises casual lunch, after-work, and errands traffic, which lifts retail-and-recreation mobility within the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT trend upward from their current levels.
